content:
oncall-bot: PAGING — p99 spike detected for canary pool 'canary-v5-quant' in us-west-2. p99 jumped from 180ms -> 2.4s over the last 6m. Auto-alert threshold breached. page: @emily (oncall).
oncall-bot: stream_stalls metric elevated on gateway-streaming, tail queue depth increased, 5xx rate @ 0.9% for canary routes.
emily: ack — I'm on it. grabbing dashboard and logs now.
sam: @emily any sign of increased CPU or OOMs on workers?
emily: CPU looks fine on nodes, but one host (gw-canary-3) shows long epoll wait and grpc stall logs: `Recv failed: Resource temporarily unavailable`.
emily: taking gw-canary-3 out of rotation for the canary pool now.
marco: re: model side — we rolled v5-quant with new KV cache layout yesterday. Could be alloc pattern causing stalls under streaming workload.
nada: (typo) ada: ^marco, that's the new kv-shadowing change we flagged. Can't rule that out.
sam: any backlog visible in batching queue? show `request_queue_length`?
emily: queue length on canary pods increased to ~120 for short bursts; normal is 5-10. batching latency spiked p95->700ms, p99->2.4s.
emily: paste logs snippet: ```
[2026-03-14T11:13:10Z] gw-canary-3 grpc: stream handler blocked for 1.9s, callid=abc123
[2026-03-14T11:13:11Z] runtime: kv-cache miss loop: waiting for lock 200ms
[2026-03-14T11:13:12Z] worker: send timeout to runtime, retrying
```
marco: that lock wait looks like contention in the new KV layout under concurrent streaming. Could cause long tail latency even if median ok.
ops-bot: Incident bot added tag: canary-rollback-proposed.
nina: customer note — Support is seeing elevated 504s for a handful of customers using streaming endpoints; tickets TKT-2241 & TKT-2242 opened. Not widespread but high-value customers affected.
emily: mitigation plan proposal: 1) divert canary traffic back to baseline model v4-stable for user-facing routes 2) scale canary pool to 0 (drain) 3) keep canary infra up for postmortem logs. Thoughts?
sam: +1 for rollback. While we investigate micro-fix we should cut traffic. What's the safest rollback path?
marco: We can change routing rule at the router layer to map canary tag -> v4-stable. That avoids infra churn. I'll prepare the routing change.
nada: ada: make sure to preserve canary traces for repro. set `trace.keep=true` for 15m before redirect.
emily: performing router change: running command: ```
/infractl route update --pool canary-v5-quant --target v4-stable --drain 30s --force
```
emily: done. routing change applied, starting in 30s window.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: route change accepted, traffic shift started.
emily: monitoring... p99 dropping. 1m after shift p99 ~140ms, p99 for streaming back to baseline.
sam: confirm no elevated error budgets for stable?
emily: stable pools unchanged, error rate normalized to ~0.1%.
nina: support update: informing impacted customers we've rerouted and are investigating root cause, offering 1 week credit where SLA affected.
marco: I'll keep canary pods in read-only mode and attach a debug runtime. Will instrument KV lock timings and run synthetic streaming load.
nada: ada: run `kvprof` with low overhead: ```
/infractl exec gw-canary-3 -- kvprof --duration 60s --freq 10ms > /tmp/kvprof.log
```
marco: started kvprof against gw-canary-3. early traces show lock hold times around 150-300ms under streaming concurrency of 60 streams. Baseline nodes show <10ms.
sam: that explains tail-only spike. We need a safe rollback + followup fix: either revert the KV layout patch or add a per-stream lock sharding. Which is quicker?
marco: reverting the KV layout is low-risk but requires a hotfix deploy on runtime images. Sharding would need code change and test. I recommend revert for immediate fix and schedule sharding as follow-up.
emily: OK oncall decision: do revert deploy for canary runtime and then re-run canary with synthetic load. planning window 15m. Paging to infra-eng for deploy.
ops-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered by @marco. build-id: 2026-03-14-canary-revert-014.
marco: roll forward revert to canary pool only. deployment plan: canary-runtime image rollback -> rolling restart of canary workers -> watch metrics 10m -> allow slow re-enable if good.
nada: ada: coordinate with SRE for paging if rollback causes regression.
sam: i'm watching p99 and queue length. keep me posted.
emily: canary revert deploy started. first pod restarted.
emily: after first 3 restarts, kv lock hold times dropped to ~8-12ms, queue length back to normal. p99 trending to 200ms and then down to baseline.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: canary image rollback complete.
emily: I'll keep canary pool drained for now and mark incident as mitigated.
nina: support update sent to customers: "We've rerouted traffic and reverted the canary runtime. Monitoring shows latency back to normal. We're performing a postmortem and will follow up."
sam: agreed next steps: 1) full postmortem 2) revert PR review to understand test coverage gap for streaming concurrency 3) add synthetic streaming perf test in CI 4) consider per-stream lock sharding.
emily: logging an incident ticket INC-2026-189 with summary and initial notes.
marco: I'll submit the revert PR reference and attach kvprof logs.
nada: can we add an alert to detect elevated kv lock hold times earlier? suggest new metric `kv.lock_hold_95` and alert at >50ms for canary routes.
sam: +1 for that alert. I'll own the alert onboarding.
emily: closing the page — mitigation successful, moving to post-incident follow-up. Thank you all. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident tag: canary-kvlock-tail.
